scope: Planner regression fix in recall_hybrid() plus three correctness fixes carried over from the 0.14.0 review: undo_consolidate() (inverse of consolidate() apply), deterministic canonical election in consolidate(), and a narrowed INCIDENT arm in classify_content_type(). No ranking algorithm change, no confidence/reinforce change, no GUC additions.
justification: Functional gate — NO recall-quality claim is made by this release, so no statistical validation is required. The recall_hybrid() change is a physical-plan fix only: the vector-candidate LIMIT was supplied from a plpgsql local variable, so PostgreSQL built a parameter-blind generic plan for RETURN QUERY, failed to recognise the small top-k pattern, and chose Seq Scan + top-N heapsort over the HNSW index scan. Passing LIMIT as a literal via EXECUTE format() restores the index scan. Result parity (identical rows, scores and ordering) was independently verified in code review — see REVIEW_0.14.1.md section 2. The improvement is in LATENCY, not in recall quality: measured on a 7440-lesson corpus, recall_hybrid() went from p50 114 ms / p95 up to 30 s (7 of 20 sample queries exceeding a 500 ms timeout) to the same order of magnitude as recall_fast(). Latency figures are engineering measurements, not a recall@k claim, and are therefore not gated on significance testing.
schema_change_detail: None — one new function (undo_consolidate) plus replacements of existing function bodies. No table, column, index or GUC changes.
scoring_impact: none — recall ranking, confidence and reinforce() paths are untouched; the recall_hybrid() fix changes only which physical execution plan the planner selects
recall_ranking_impact: none — result parity independently confirmed in code review (same rows, same scores, same ordering)
backward_compat_proof: pg_regress test_v0141_hnsw_planner pins the planner fix, test_v0141_p1b pins the classifier and canonical-election behaviour, undo_consolidate pins consolidate/undo round-trip. Existing 0.14.0 fixtures continue to pass unchanged. Upgrade path is incremental (0.14.0→0.14.1) or fresh-install.

corpus.note: functional gate only; latency measurements were taken on a 7440-row corpus during diagnosis, but this release makes no recall-quality claim and therefore requires no statistical validation
